subtitle: Organizing early network data sharing research.

tldr.problem: The early ARPANET community needed to coordinate research on how computers could share and manage data across the network.
tldr.mechanism: A new Network Data Management Committee was formed, chaired by Doug McKay of IBM, to classify issues, integrate separate activities, and coordinate experiments in network data sharing.
tldr.outcome: The committee held meetings to gather position papers from sites on data sharing approaches and set up a coordinated research program.

today: RFC 173 is a historic coordination announcement for early network research. Its role was to establish a research committee; the actual data sharing protocols that emerged from this effort were documented in later RFCs.

sections.title: The Data Management Challenge
sections.content:
RFC 173 announces the formation of the Network Data Management Committee, created following data discussions at an NWG meeting in May 1971. The committee was chaired by Doug McKay of IBM.

The committee's purpose, established in RFC 146, was threefold: to classify the issues involved in network data sharing, to integrate the separate network activities addressing data sharing problems, and to set up and coordinate experiments to test the services developed.
sections.plainLanguage: The early network needed a team to figure out how machines could safely swap information. They chose a leader and listed what they wanted to tackle.

sections.title: Committee Organization and Topics
sections.content:
An informal meeting was held on Wednesday, 19 May 1971 to establish an approach for the committee's work. Attendees included representatives from MITRE, IBM, Raytheon, UCLA, ARPA, and CCA (Computer Corporation of America).

The committee planned to hold a data management meeting at CCA in Cambridge prior to the next NWG meeting, similar in structure to the network graphics meeting described in RFC 87. Sites were asked to submit working papers on selected topics, including philosophical discussions of network data sharing, syntax and semantics for data description and access languages, approaches for integrating existing data handling services, experimentation methodology, network data directory design, and operational control protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: Leaders from different research sites met to plan. They would ask each site to write papers about their ideas on how to manage shared information.

sections.title: Meeting Schedule and Call for Papers
sections.content:
Position papers were due to Doug McKay by 16 July 1971, with a deadline of 19 July for receipt. The committee planned to distribute a meeting agenda, copies of all papers, and a background bibliography by 23 July. The data management meeting was scheduled for 2 August to 4 August 1971 at CCA, located at 565 Technology Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Participants were asked to contact Marty Ginsberg at CCA by 16 July for hotel reservations.
sections.plainLanguage: They set deadlines for papers, scheduled a meeting time and place, and asked sites to arrange their travel.
